card.title: ILYUSHIN IL-2
card.text: Deployment: Choose a unit in hand with a cost of 3 or less. Put it into play.
card.flavorText: The Ilyushin IL-2, also known as the Sturmovik, entered Soviet service in 1941 as a heavily armored single-seat ground-attack aircraft. Designed to support troops at the front, it featured a steel armored shell integrated into the fuselage to protect the pilot, engine, and fuel tanks. This innovative structure made the IL-2 more resilient than most aircraft of its time. Armed with 23 mm cannons, bombs, and unguided rockets, it became a key asset in the Soviet Union’s response to the German invasion. Despite its strong defensive design, the single-seat IL-2 had critical weaknesses. Lacking a rear gunner, it was highly vulnerable to enemy fighters. Inexperienced pilots and ground crews faced a steep learning curve, and early losses were severe. Nonetheless, the aircraft proved effective in battlefield roles, especially against convoys and soft targets. Soviet pilots developed tactics that emphasized sloped dive attacks and concentrated fire. Production was initially slow due to wartime factory relocations, but output increased rapidly after Stalin’s personal intervention. By late 1942, improvements began to appear, including the transition to a two-seat design. However, the original single-seat IL-2 set the foundation for what would become the most produced military aircraft design in history.
